intro: Discovery window 2016-10 to 2022 only, 34 instruments, daily London-session holds at equal ex-post vol; 663 cells tested, 213 pass BH at q = 0.10 (about 21.3 of those expected false).

Steadier risk HOLDS ACROSS everything: sizing by the forecast sigma brings monthly risk closer to target in every class, year, regime and tercile (pooled 0.1524 vs 0.263 unscaled), and survives a one-session delay (-0.103 [-0.137, -0.075]). A broad plateau, not a peak: exponent 0.75-1.25 all work. Trailing RV20 does exactly as well (late: -0.0019 [-0.0093, +0.0050]); RV10 is steadier still (0.1284) but has more tail days.

The tail REVERSES by vol level: sigma sizing does not cut tail days overall (0.928% vs 1.06%), it MOVES them. High-sigma days: 2.484% -> 0.446% beyond 3 sd; low-sigma days: 0.204% -> 1.476%, p99 loss -2.029 -> -2.876 sd. Calm years (2017-19, 2021) get MORE tail days, loud years (2020, 2022) fewer. A quiet-day surprise is held at full size.

C.OG's jump allowance as built here (trailing rv - bv jump variance) changes nothing: it scales with sigma, so the size barely moves (low-sigma tail 1.476% vs 1.476%). A level allowance that does not shrink with today's vol, sqrt(sigma^2 + 0.25 x trailing median sigma^2), cuts low-sigma tail days to 1.19% (late: -0.31pp [-0.43, -0.20]) for +0.002 steadiness, but adds tail days on loud days. It was added after seeing the data: stage 4 must confirm it.
1/sigma^2 (Moreira-Muir) is worse everywhere: unsteadier (0.2676), more tail days (1.415%; 3.707% on low-sigma days). Over 5-session holds no sizing differs from another (0 of 15 cells).

The book is mostly the dollar, and more so when the dollar is loud: R2 of the 14-leg book on the dollar factor 0.62 (shuffled 0.489), 0.475 in 2017 to 0.766 in 2022; 0.499 in the quietest dollar-vol tercile vs 0.714 in the loudest. Leg-level ERC does not change this (USD share 0.5 vs 0.496, ES diff +0.000 [-0.059, +0.072]).

All-correlations-to-1 stress: the model 99% VaR is breached 2.07% of days (1% nominal), the stress figure 0.19%. As a cap on the book vol target (stressed sd <= 2x target, binds 20% of days) it keeps the steadier risk (0.194 vs 0.202) and trims the worst day (-4.49 vs -4.79 sd), but ES 1% does not move (+0.04 [-0.09, +0.25]) and the worst-day gain is gone with a one-session delay (-4.98 vs -4.82).

Stops on the M1 bid/ask path: a 1-sigma stop from the open is touched 32.45% net and 29.77% on the mid (random walk 31.73%); entering later with sigma scaled to the session's remaining variance keeps the net rate at 32.14-32.57% in every bucket. Turbulent regime 28.54% vs calm 32.95%: sigma over-reacts after loud stretches. Gap-through fills are tiny on M1 (net p99 1.001-1.008R): the one-step loss lives in the daily tail, not in the stop fill.

charts.title: Per instrument: how far monthly realised risk strays from target
charts.note: Daily London-session hold at equal ex-post vol per instrument; bar = average distance of a month's realised vol from the target (0 = perfectly steady). Benchmark: the unscaled bar, and trailing RV20 for the chosen sigma. Forecast sigma beats unscaled in 34/34 and RV20 in 15/34. Sigma + jump allowance is within 0.002 of forecast sigma everywhere (not drawn).

charts.title: p99 loss of the daily hold by class and sigma tercile (equal ex-post vol)
charts.note: More negative = a worse 1-in-100 day at the same average risk. Benchmark: unscaled, and -2.33 for a normal. Forecast - unscaled p99, by class: FX majors -0.00 [-0.26, +0.31]; FX crosses +0.03 [-0.16, +0.22]; metals +0.30 [-0.40, +0.95]; indices -0.15 [-0.57, +0.27]; low sigma -0.85 [-0.95, -0.76]. Loss-tail shape (GPD xi above the 95th pct loss, 200 date-block resamples; normal draws give -0.121): unscaled 0.133 [0.022, 0.2], forecast sigma 0.093 [0.029, 0.14], sigma + jump allowance 0.1 [0.033, 0.14], sigma + level allowance 0.093 [0.029, 0.144], 1/sigma^2 0.141 [0.081, 0.19]. RV20 and the jump allowance sit within 0.03 of forecast sigma (facts file).

charts.title: Year by year: distance of monthly risk from target (34 instruments pooled)
charts.note: Each year's instrument-months, same equal-vol scaling. Benchmark: unscaled. A sizing that holds across sits low every year; 2020 is the stress test. Beyond-3-sd days by year (unscaled / forecast): 2017 0.674/0.982%, 2018 0.273/0.797%, 2019 0.489/1.001%, 2020 2.584/0.997%, 2021 0.249/0.997%, 2022 2.082/0.853% - sigma sizing adds tail days in calm years.

charts.title: Where the tail days land: beyond 3 sd by vol regime and sigma tercile
charts.note: Regime = C.OG Lesson 05 (63-session vol > 1.25 x its rolling median for 21+ sessions, past only): 103 turbulent episodes, median 57 sessions, 11% of days; intervals use blocks of 57 sessions. Terciles of the forecast sigma within each instrument. Benchmark: unscaled, and 0.27% for a normal. Unscaled tails pile into loud days; sigma sizing moves them into quiet days (low sigma: forecast - unscaled +1.27pp [+1.02, +1.55]), because a quiet-day surprise is now held at full size. Level allowance - forecast in low sigma: -0.29pp [-0.38, -0.19].

charts.title: Plateau check: size = 1/sigma^p (p 0 to 2) and the RV window
charts.note: Same holds, same equal ex-post vol; only the exponent moves. Benchmark: p = 0 (unscaled). Read the risk-deviation line for a flat floor around p = 1 (plateau) vs a single dip (peak), and the tail line for where tail days are fewest. The trailing-RV series (x = window/60: 5..120 sessions) shows the same for the RV window. Values: p=0 dev 0.263 tail 1.06%, p=0.25 dev 0.2173 tail 0.919%, p=0.5 dev 0.1799 tail 0.882%, p=0.75 dev 0.1564 tail 0.867%, p=1.0 dev 0.1524 tail 0.928%, p=1.25 dev 0.1676 tail 1.029%, p=1.5 dev 0.1956 tail 1.174%, p=2.0 dev 0.2676 tail 1.415%; RV 5d 0.1519, 10d 0.1284, 20d 0.151, 40d 0.1887, 60d 0.2022, 120d 0.2213.

charts.title: All-correlations-to-1 stress cap on the book vol target (Lesson 06)
charts.unit: book sd at equal ex-post vol
charts.note: The book vol target levers the equal-risk book by 1/model vol (median 1.7x, 5-95%: 1.28-2.38). The stress figure assumes every correlation is 1, so the stressed sd is the sum of leg risks; the cap keeps stressed sd <= L x target. L = 1 is the plain equal-risk book, 'none' is the uncapped target. Benchmarks: both ends. Capped - uncapped ES 1%: L=1.5 -0.01 [-0.31, +0.36]; L=2.0 +0.04 [-0.09, +0.25]; L=3.0 -0.00 [-0.00, +0.00].

charts.title: 99% VaR breaches of the equal-risk book: model correlation vs all-to-1 stress
charts.note: Benchmark: 1% (a calibrated 99% VaR). The model figure breaches far too often in crashes because correlation jumps on the day; the stress figure almost never breaches, so it is a cap, not a forecast. Regime = Lesson 05 on the book's own vol. Worst book days (sd of model): 2018-02-05 -4.68, 2020-06-11 -3.92, 2022-09-13 -3.15.

At equal vol: ES 1% ERC -3.3 vs -3.301 sd (diff +0.000 [-0.059, +0.072]); monthly risk deviation diff +0.0113 [+0.0018, +0.0209]; HHI of risk shares 2022: inverse vol 0.0733, ERC 0.0718 (equal = 0.0714).

charts.title: Time of day: 1 x sigma_remaining stop touched, on the M1 bid/ask path
names: net (enter at offer/bid, stop on the far side)
charts.note: Entry at each London bucket's start, long and short, held to 22:00. Stop = 1 x the session sigma x sqrt(share of the session's variance still to come, from the trailing 250-session intraday profile, past only). Benchmark: a random walk touches 31.73%. Later entries have smaller stops, so the spread is a bigger part of 1R (label).

charts.title: What a 1R stop really costs: realised loss when stopped (from the open, k = 1)
charts.note: Fill = the stop, or the bar's opening bid/offer if price gapped through it (the one-step loss C.OG's Lesson 03 warns sizing on vol misses). Benchmark: 1.0R (a perfect stop). Net: entry at the offer/bid, stop 1R from that fill, triggered on the far side of the quote; loss = cash lost / planned 1R (the spread shows up as extra touches, chart above). Gross: the same on the mid path. 765 entries whose remaining session had a data hole > 30 min were dropped (a hole would fake a gap-through). Max net loss by class: FX majors 1.06R, FX crosses 1.74R, metals 1.38R, indices 1.1R.

charts.title: Does 1R stay 1R on bid/ask? 1-sigma stop from the open, by year
charts.note: Net = bid/ask path with the entry spread; gross = mid path (what stage 2 measured on session H/L). Benchmark: random walk 31.73%. Regime (Lesson 05): calm 32.95% net, turbulent 28.54% net [26.86, 29.72].

charts.title: Real gap-through stops: 1R planned, more lost (bid/ask, from the open)
charts.note: Entry at the London open at the offer (long) or bid (short), stop 1 x sigma away (dashed). Path = the exit side (bid for longs, offer for shorts), 10-minute samples plus the touch bar. Benchmark: a perfect stop loses exactly 1R. These are the largest gap-through fills (one per class first): real ones are rare and small - see the loss chart.
